en:
So I'm up second?
All right, then, let's get to it.
My name's Makoto Shindo.
Good to meet you.
So, you ever heard the story of 'the Candy Granny'?
The Candy Granny was an old woman who used to stand outside the students' side gate back in the day.
Supposedly she was still around until five or six years ago.
They say she was pretty famous.
I only heard about her from an upperclassman, see.
I never actually saw her myself.
I bet the teachers all still know about her, though, don't you think?
This Candy Granny, she dressed just like a witch who rides around on a broomstick.{p}

She wore a bright red hooded robe with the hood up, summer and winter alike.
On her big hooked nose sat a huge wart, like a bean.
Her chin was pointed like a crescent moon, and her whole face was covered in wrinkles.
When she smiled, they say you'd catch glimpses of a freakishly long red tongue in her almost toothless mouth.
In one hand she leaned on a gnarled wooden cane, and from the other hung a big basket.
See?
Just like the old witch in a fairy tale, right?
But here's the thing: she looked scary, but supposedly she was kind.
She'd stand by the gate, and when she spotted a kid she liked, or a lonely kid all on their own, she'd walk right up to them.{p}

Then, from the ratty, grimy basket hanging from her skeleton of a hand, all skin and bone, a basket crammed full of candies, she'd give them one.
That's how she got the nickname 'the Candy Granny.'
And they say those candies were insanely good.
Each one was the size of a golf ball, so big it filled your whole mouth, and the taste of it...
It's like it melts all through your mouth, or makes you lose track of time, or something. Not too sweet, but not too bland either.
A perfectly balanced harmony of deliciousness.
Just thinking about it is enough to make my mouth water.{p}

Well, not that I've ever eaten one myself.
It's only a rumor, but doesn't it sound good?{p}Would you want to try one too?
I'd like to try one
I'd rather not

Right? I knew it.
I totally get how you feel.
I'm not that into sweets, but I love anything that tastes good.
The candy came in crumpled plastic with no brand name or anything on it, so at first most kids didn't want it.
Even after getting one, most of them just threw it away.{p}

I mean, you can't blame them.
Some creepy old woman hands you a mystery candy.
You've got no idea what's in it, and for all you know it's poison.
Normally, you'd toss it, right?
Still, there's always some weirdo out there.
Somebody actually ate one.
Word is, the first one who ate that candy got bullied like crazy and had been thinking about killing themselves for ages.{p}

So they figured even poison would be fine, and ate the candy ready to die.
And guess what?
That candy was good. So, so good.
It tasted like nothing from this world.
Like, "There's something this delicious in the world?"
And that gave them the courage to keep living.{p}

After that, they started fighting back when they got bullied, and on top of that they turned so cheerful you wouldn't even recognize them.
Then after graduating high school they went to culinary school, and now I hear they're the chef at a three-star restaurant in France.
One single candy changed a person's whole life.
Well, it's only a rumor, mind you. A rumor.
Still, pretty amazing story, huh?{p}
Well?{p}Now you want to meet the Candy Granny, don't you?
I want to meet her
Not particularly

Yeah, yeah.
I know just how you feel.{p}

So anyway, about this Candy Granny.
For some reason, once she'd given someone a candy, she'd never show herself to them again.
Remember the kid I told you about?
The one who's a chef in France now.
Even they couldn't forget the taste of that candy, so they went looking for the Candy Granny.{p}

They figured if they waited at the side gate they'd meet her, so they waited, but no matter how long they waited, she never showed up.
And yet the moment they left, she'd appear out of nowhere and give a candy to somebody else.
Weird, right?
Apparently they searched all over the place, but never found her.
Even when they heard she was at the side gate right then and rushed over, she'd already be gone.
Like she was running away from them.{p}

Still, it worked out for the best.
I mean, a chef in France.
Seriously impressive.
After that, the Candy Granny turned into a bit of a celebrity.
There was always a crowd at the side gate, waiting for her.
Like people chasing after some TV star.
It looked like she was about to get her own fan club.
Everyone was there just to get a taste of her candy.
Then again, you could say it was only candy, and that'd be the end of it.{p}

But for some reason, she never showed up when there were lots of people around.
Once everyone figured she wasn't coming anymore and stopped gathering, she'd show up out of nowhere.
And she'd give a candy to some lonely kid.
People hear about it, and the crowd gathers again.
But she doesn't show.
Then when the people leave...
Over and over, like that.{p}

But the reason everyone wanted that candy wasn't just that it tasted good.
Sure, there were probably some simple types who just wanted to try candy that good, but what everyone was really after was the life they'd have after eating it.
For some reason, anyone who ate that candy suddenly turned cheerful.
Just like that kid who became a chef in France.
They'd get this weird confidence, or something, and succeed at whatever they tried.
Kids who were bad at studying suddenly got great grades, and kids with no coordination suddenly turned into star athletes.
And then a rosy school life was waiting for them.
Sounds like a dream, huh?
It got to where people whispered, like it was the plain truth, that the Candy Granny was a real witch and a friend to the weak.{p}
Apparently plenty of people believed that rumor.{p}You'd really love a taste of the Candy Granny's candy, wouldn't you?
I'd love a taste
I wouldn't

I'd say the same.
You're an honest one.
If there's a candy like magic, anybody who says they wouldn't want a taste is a liar.
So anyway, there was this guy named Noboru Sakuma.{p}

He wasn't good with people, or rather, he was just selfish.
The type who can't stand it when things don't go his way.
The type who thinks the world revolves around him.
Not that he was anybody special. Just a nasty piece of work, right?
Well, I never actually met him either, so it's only a rumor, ha ha ha...
Anyway, on the surface he acted like he wasn't interested.{p}

"Are you guys idiots or what?
Why are you all worked up over one stupid candy?
Bunch of little kids, seriously."
That's the kind of thing he said.
Of course, deep down he wanted it like crazy.
That magic candy.
Everyone could see that, so nobody bothered with Sakuma.
I wouldn't want to hang out with a contrary jerk like that either.{p}

So Sakuma was always waiting near the school for the Candy Granny, they say.
Making sure nobody spotted him.
Man, he must've been dying for it.
Rain, wind, even snow, he waited, hiding in the shadow of a telephone pole.
Like a detective on a stakeout on TV.
If he had that much grit, he should've just become a detective.
Sakuma waited.
He kept on waiting, desperately.
That's how bad he wanted that candy.{p}

"All by yourself, are you, dearie?"
Just as he was about to leave, someone suddenly spoke to him from behind.{p}

He turned around, and what do you know, there stood an old lady with a red hood pulled low over her eyes.
It was the Candy Granny.
There hadn't been anyone there a moment ago, but she'd appeared like a puff of smoke.
"Ah, the Candy Granny!"
Sakuma couldn't help shouting.
The old lady laughed, a nasty sound like fingernails scraping glass.

"...Ee-hee-hee... That I am.
You've been waiting for me, haven't you, dearie?"{p}What do you think Sakuma said?
I was waiting for you
I wasn't really waiting

"...Not really.
I was just wandering around."
That's Sakuma for you, the contrarian.
He'd finally met the Candy Granny he'd been dying to see, and he still had to act tough.
Even so, the old lady laughed, as if she saw right through him.{p}

"Is that so?
Children like you are just the kind I'm fond of.
You've gotten so twisted, you must have led a truly miserable life, eh?"
After hearing that, how could Sakuma not get ticked off?{p}

"Shut up, will ya.
I wasn't waiting for you!
Just get lost already!"
Things he didn't mean kept slipping out of his mouth.
He always thought, oh crap, right after he said them, but by then it was too late.
That's why he kept screwing everything up.
Even after Sakuma said all that to her, the old lady just kept laughing.{p}

"Don't be so cold, dearie.
I only ever appear before you once, you know.
Just once in your whole long life.
Don't you think it'd be a waste to throw that away yourself?"
The old lady knew.
She knew Sakuma needed her.{p}So what do you think Sakuma did?
Says he wanted to meet her
Brushes her off coldly

Sakuma really was a complete idiot.
"It's not a waste!
It's my life, I'll live it however I damn well want!
I don't need some total stranger like you telling me what to do!"
The old lady should've just left a punk like that alone.{p}

Who knows why, though.
The old lady showed no sign of leaving at all.
"What a sweet child.
Why can't you be honest with yourself, I wonder?
A child like you ought to have a nice, tasty candy.
It's a very, very tasty candy, you know."{p}

Without Sakuma even asking, the old lady plucked one big candy out of the basket hanging from her hand.
Sakuma gulped.
The truth was, he wanted it so badly he could hardly stand it.
And that candy was right in front of him.
All he had to do was reach out and say thank you, and it'd be his.
And his life would change.
But an idiot's an idiot to the bitter end.
He wanted it, and still he acted like he didn't.{p}

He turned his face away and said, like it was a huge pain,
"...Well, if you're that desperate for me to take it, granny, I guess I could take it off your hands.
But if it tastes bad, you'll be sorry."
Even while he mouthed off, Sakuma snatched the candy out of the old lady's hand.
Then he tore off the wrapper and hurriedly popped it into his mouth.{p}
What a taste!

He'd never tasted anything like it in his life.
The rumors were true.
"Is it good?"
"...It's good!"
At the old lady's words, Sakuma let the truth slip out.
It was good enough to make even a contrarian like Sakuma groan.
But right after he said it, he thought, oh crap.
It ticked him off.
That he'd gone and done exactly what the old lady wanted.
And at the same time, a different desire began to bubble up inside him.
Yeah.{p}

It was the desire for more candy.
Then, on reflex, he shoved his hand into the old lady's basket and stole some candy.
"What are you doing!"
Ignoring her cries to stop, Sakuma shoved the old lady away and ran.{p}

"...What the hell.
Only two?"
The candies were big, after all.
Two was all he could manage to grab.
Still, Sakuma was pretty satisfied.{p}

When he got home, he shut himself in his room and lined up the two candies on his desk.
Everyone else only got to taste one.
But he got to taste three.
So his life ought to be three times as fun, too.{p}
Thinking that, he couldn't help laughing.

Looking at the candies, that taste from before came flooding back.
His mouth filled with spit.
A taste he couldn't forget even if he tried.
The taste was so vivid he almost felt like it was still in his mouth.
"This is killing me."
Just looking at them, he couldn't hold back.
Still, he only had two left.
He couldn't eat them now.
"...Maybe just a little lick."
He couldn't resist the temptation.
No way a selfish guy like him could.
Meaning to take just one tiny lick, he brought a candy to his mouth.{p}

"...This is killing me.
It's way too good!"
He meant to take it out of his mouth right away, but he just couldn't stop.
The candy, big as it had been, melted away in no time.
And once he'd eaten one, there was no stopping him.{p}

"I can't hold back anymore!"
Sakuma reached for the last one and hurriedly tossed it into his mouth.
That was the happiest moment Sakuma ever had.
He must have thought he could die happy right then.
After all, he'd tasted three times a flavor even the chosen ones only got to taste once.
He knew that once it was gone he'd never eat another, but he couldn't spit it out.
He wanted to save it, but the urge for just a little more, just a little more won out, and before he knew it, the last candy had slid down into his stomach too.
"Haaaaaah."
Sakuma had never felt such satisfaction.
It was a moment of pure bliss.

That's when it happened.
There was a knock at his door.{p}

"Shut up already.
I'm studying right now.
I don't want a late-night snack."
Thinking it was his mother, who always brought him a snack at night, Sakuma answered curtly.{p}

"...Give them back.
...Give me back my candies."
He jumped.
His heart nearly stopped.
That voice was, without a doubt, the Candy Granny's.
He had no idea why she was here.
This was Sakuma's own room, after all.
There was no way his family would let an old lady like that into the house.
How had she gotten inside? It gave him the creeps.
"...Come now, give them back.
Those are my precious candies, they are."
The old lady's voice came through the door, full of bitter resentment.
She wanted her candies back, but he'd already eaten them.{p}What was he supposed to do?
Open the door
Leave the door shut

Sakuma was creeped out beyond belief.
His gut told him he must not let her in, no matter what.

"...Come on, give them back to me."
"Aaagh!"
Sakuma screamed at the top of his lungs.
The old lady's voice had come from right behind him.{p}

He turned around, and there stood the old lady. How she'd gotten in, he had no idea.
In a panic he looked at the door. It was locked tight.
And it hit Sakuma all over again.
This old lady wasn't human.{p}

"...S-stop it, please.
It was my fault.
Forgive me!"
Sakuma was scared, so scared, and he apologized for all he was worth.
But the old lady wasn't listening to a word Sakuma said.
"Do you like candy?"
"I-I'm sorry.
I won't do it again!"
No matter how hard Sakuma apologized, the old lady paid no mind and fired one question after another at him.
"Do you want candy?"
"Was the candy good?"
"How many candies did you eat?"
Sakuma didn't answer her questions. He just kept on apologizing, over and over.{p}

The old lady brought her wrinkled face right up to Sakuma's and grinned a nasty grin.
And then she said,
"...Come now, give me back my candies."
"I'm sorry!
They're gone!
I ate them!"
The old lady grabbed Sakuma's trembling face with incredible strength and stared at it, long and hard.{p}

"What are you talking about?
You've still got them right here.
Two lovely eyeballs, so tasty-looking..."

...The whole room was a sea of blood.
The old lady was nowhere to be seen.
There was only Sakuma, alone in the middle of the room, rolling around on the floor and clutching his bloody face.
"My eyes...!
My eyes hurt!"
His shocked mother pried his hands away from his face, and... his eyes were gone.
Where his eyes should have been, there was nothing but gaping black holes.{p}

After that, Sakuma lost his mind, and I hear he dropped out of school.
It was after that, see,
that the Candy Granny stopped showing up.
But for the past few years, they say a man in sunglasses has been turning up now and then at the students' side gate.
Whenever he gets the chance, he stops a student, takes off his sunglasses, and...{p}

"...Give me back my eyeballs.
They weren't candy, you know.
...Please, give them back to me."
That's what he says, sobbing in a thin little voice.
The guy has no eyes, they say. Just two pitch-black holes.{p}

You've never met him, right?
No telling when you might.
Watch yourself.
...By the way, {a}.{p}A little while ago, you said you wanted to meet the Candy Granny and eat her candy, didn't you?
I said that
I never said that

Don't lie to me.
I heard you, plain as day.
They say anyone who hears this story and says they want to eat the Candy Granny's candy gets to meet her.
Sometime in the next month, somewhere, you'll run into her.
Whether it's in a crowd or in your own room, I couldn't tell you.
And she'll hold out that delicious candy and ask you some questions.
"Do you like candy?"
"Do you want candy?"
"Was the candy good?"
"How many candies did you eat?"
Four questions, just like that.{p}

Now listen, and listen good.
This is how you answer those questions.
I'm only gonna say it once.
"Do you like candy?"
If she asks you that,
"I hate it."
That's your answer.
"Do you want candy?"
If she asks you that,
"I don't want any."
That's your answer.
"Was the candy good?"
If she asks you that,
"Sakuma's the one who ate the candy."
That's your answer.
"How many candies did you eat?"
If she asks you that,
"Sakuma ate three."
That's what you tell her.
Got it? Don't you dare get it wrong.
If you try to run, or give the wrong answer to any of those questions, she'll gouge your eyes out.
And then your eyeballs get turned into candy.{p}

Well, it's only a month you've gotta hold out.
Just tough it out.
...That's the end of my story.
Let's have the next one tell theirs.{p}

You don't wanna eat it?
It's crazy good, I'm telling you.
And that candy isn't just tasty, either.
Well? You wanna try it, don't you?
I'll keep asking as many times as it takes.{p}Me, I sure wanna eat it.
I want to eat it
I don't want to eat it

You don't want to?
What are you talking about?{p}Deep down you really wanna try it, don't you?
I want to eat it
I don't want to eat it

Huh?
You're more stubborn than you look.
You're the first one who's ever heard this story and said they didn't wanna eat it.
Or maybe...{p}Don't tell me you hate candy?
I like candy
I hate candy

I see...
So you hate candy.
Well then, I guess it can't be helped...
But y'know, no matter how much someone hates candy, I bet they'd say the Candy Granny's candy, at least, is absolutely delicious.
They say there was someone like that among the people who got her candy, too.
I think the story went something like this...{p}

Satoko Katagiri, a first-year back then, was nobody you'd call a beauty, and she sure wasn't slim either.
What do you call it, pear-shaped?
She had a huge sweet tooth, and pretty much every day she ate snacks and cake from morning till night.
And the result...
Well, naturally, she ended up with terrible cavities.
For a good while she couldn't eat sweets, or even regular meals.
Then one day...{p}

"Ah, the Candy Granny!"
She had a sweet tooth, remember.
Of course she knew the rumors about the Candy Granny.
"You like sweet things, don't you, dearie?
Here, let me give you this."{p}
The Candy Granny picked one big ball of candy out of the basket hanging from her arm and pressed it into Katagiri's hand.{p}

"It's delicious candy.
So good your cheeks will fall right off."
With that, the old lady twisted her wrinkled mouth into a smile.
"Candy...?"

The moment she thought it, a stabbing pain shot through the back of Katagiri's head.
Cavities, y'know...{p}

Just picturing something sweet makes them start hurting like crazy, right?
That's rough, man.
What about you, {a}?{p}Have you ever had a rough time with a cavity?
Yes, I have
No, never

So...
"Who wants this stupid thing!"
she yelled, and threw the candy away.
I guess she just snapped.
The old lady must've been startled by how furious she was.
"Eeeeeeek!"
she cried, and went hopping and bouncing off somewhere.{p}

"Ugh! She has no idea what I'm going through..."
Just then, Katagiri's best friend, Eriko Hara, happened by.
"Satoko! What's got you all huffy?"
"Well, actually..."
And she told her everything that had just happened.
"Whaaat?!
You threw away the Candy Granny's candy★"
"Don't talk so loud.
It hurts my teeth."
"What are you saying?!
What a waste!
That candy, see..."
Put simply, what Hara told her goes like this.{p}

The Candy Granny's candy isn't just delicious.
They say everyone who's ever sucked on one has found happiness, without fail.
You get this weird surge of confidence or something, and whatever you try, it works out.
Kids who were bad at studying suddenly get great grades, and kids with no coordination suddenly turn into star athletes.
And then a rosy school life is waiting for them.
Sounds like a dream, huh?{p}

"...Whaaat★"
Katagiri frantically searched around where she'd thrown the candy.
But there was nothing like it anywhere.
After that, Katagiri kept waiting for the Candy Granny, pretty much every day.
In the end, though, she graduated without ever seeing her again.{p}

What a waste, blowing a chance like that, huh?
And get this: no matter how many times her cavities get fixed, her teeth rot away again in no time.
Rumor is she's still going to the dentist even now.
I bet that's her punishment for treating the Candy Granny's candy like trash, don't you think?
She missed her shot at good luck, and her cavities never get better. Talk about adding insult to injury.
This year's my last chance too, but...
Well, I'll look for her without getting my hopes up.
If you ever do meet the Candy Granny, you're in luck.
After all, it's magic candy.
...Oh wait, you hate candy, don't you, {a}?
Then when that happens, give it to me.
Whatever you do, don't go wasting it by throwing it away like Katagiri did.
Got it?
Alright, that's the end of my story.
Who's up next?{p}

After all this, you're gonna say that?
...Well, whatever.
You're saying you'll grab your happiness with your own two hands, is that it?
Maybe that's not so bad either.
But y'know, in the end there's only so much a human being can do.
Sure, it's fine to push yourself and chase dreams that'll never come true.
But the people who actually make their dreams come true that way are just a tiny handful.
You really don't want much, do you?
But if that's what you say, then fine by me.
Among the people who got the candy, there's a story like this too...{p}

Satoko Katagiri, a first-year back then, was nobody you'd call a beauty, and she sure wasn't slim either.
What do you call it, pear-shaped?
But she was a sweet kid, and I think people liked her well enough.
She had a best friend named Eriko Hara.
This girl was cute enough, but her personality was super nasty.
Everyone used to say, "How do those two even stand hanging out together?"
Not that I saw it myself or anything.
Katagiri was basically just there to make Hara look good.
And I bet Hara felt superior about it and was perfectly happy that way.
Seriously, what a nasty piece of work.
One day, after school, Katagiri was waiting at the school gate for Hara, who had cleaning duty.{p}

"Are you waiting for someone, dearie?"
"Y-yes, just a friend."
Katagiri got a little spooked.
Then again, anybody would get spooked if an old lady who looked like that suddenly spoke up from behind them.
"Well then, before that friend of yours comes, there's something I want to give you.
Here, this is it."{p}

"I can see you've got a kind heart, dearie.
A child like you ought to be much happier than this.
I'll take away that handicap that keeps dogging you.

Hee hee hee hee."
"Uh... okay..."{p}

With that, the old lady went hopping and bouncing off somewhere.
"What was that about? That old lady..."
"Satoko! What's with you, spacing out like that?"
"Well, actually..."
And she told her everything that had just happened.{p}

"And this is it."
"Ew, gross! Why would you take something like that?
Hurry up and throw it away."
"Yeah, but I think I'll hang onto it anyway.
Something about it bugs me..."
"Ugh, do whatever you want.
If you're keeping it, then put it away already. It's creepy."
Katagiri shoved the candy into her bag...{p}

Then, while she and Hara were busy chatting about silly stuff, she forgot all about the old lady.
When Katagiri got home and was going over the next day's lessons...{p}

"Huh, did I take this out of my bag?"
The candy was sitting on the right-hand edge of her desk.
"It must've fallen out earlier when I took my notebook out."
She picked up the candy and thought about the old lady.
"But she didn't give me a bad feeling at all.
I wonder why...
Oh, well.
I'm hungry, so maybe I'll just have it."
And she went for it and popped it right into her mouth.{p}

"Oh my gosh, this is sooo delicious!
It makes me glad to be alive!
Good thing I didn't throw it away!"
She savored it to the very end, and then, still feeling happy, she went to sleep without even brushing her teeth.
That was when the strange things started.{p}

"Hey, Satoko.
Have you lost weight or something?"
"I know, right?!
I'm not dieting or doing anything special, but I just keep getting thinner."
That's right. She slimmed right down, and her skin got all smooth too.
Weird, huh?
And she got so pretty you wouldn't even recognize her.
"Hey, Katagiri's gotten kinda pretty, huh?"
Her popularity with the boys shot through the roof.
The one who wasn't happy about it was Hara, I bet.{p}

One day, Hara cornered Katagiri.
"There's some secret, isn't there?
Come on, tell me☆{p}We're best friends, aren't we?"
Tell her the truth
Don't tell her

"Sure.
Hey, Eriko, don't you remember?
That old lady?
It's all thanks to the candy she gave me that day."
And she told her everything that had happened since she ate the candy.
"I see. So that's how it is."
Hara grinned slyly.{p}

After that, day after day, Hara waited for the Candy Granny at the school gate.
Rain, wind, even snow, she waited, hiding in the shadow of a telephone pole.
If she had that much grit, she could've spent the time working on herself and gotten a lot prettier, y'know.
Hara waited.
She kept on waiting, desperately.{p}

"No luck today either..."
The sun had gone down completely, and there were no students left heading home from school.
Hara pinned her hopes on tomorrow once again and decided to go home.

"All by yourself, are you, dearie?"
Just as she was about to leave, someone suddenly spoke to her from behind.{p}

She turned around, and what do you know, there stood an old lady with a red hood pulled low over her eyes.
It was the Candy Granny.
There hadn't been anyone there a moment ago, but she'd appeared like a puff of smoke.
"Y-you're the Candy Granny, aren't you!"
The old lady glided right up to Hara and spoke, all but pressing her warty nose into her face.

"...Ee-hee-hee... That I am.
You've been waiting for me, haven't you, dearie?"
"...Not really.
I was just wandering around, that's all."
This was Hara we're talking about, with her not-so-cute personality, so of course she put on a tough front.
Even so, the old lady laughed as if she could see right through her.

"Is that so?
That's just the kind of child I'm fond of.
So pretty, and yet your nature is the very opposite, eh?
Those looks are the only thing you've got going for you."

Hara couldn't help bristling at that.
"Who's the one who isn't cute here?
Whatever, just hurry up and hand over the candy already☆"
Hara practically tore a candy out of the old lady's basket and ran off.{p}

"My, my, what an impatient child.
Well, I suppose that's that child's fate as well..."{p}

When Hara got home, she hurried to her room and locked the door.
"I can't wait to see everyone's surprised faces. Hee hee."
Then she slowly sucked on the candy.
A few days later...{p}

They say her eyes slanted up, her mouth bent down into a scowl, deep creases dug in between her brows, and her whole face warped into something mean.
Just like Hara's heart, see.
Apparently the candies the old lady hands out come in different kinds.
They say she picks out the candy that suits each person.
That's why things work out pretty well for everyone, I guess.
